title: the birth of the cousins
hook: the three brothers grow up, the pale one is crowned, and a princess of Gandhara learns her husband is blind and ties a cloth over her own eyes
carry: a strip of cloth, folded and tied

segments.voice: Yesterday: Pandu the pale, and Vidura, the maid's son. She simply showed him respect.

A strip of cloth, folded over and over, tied behind the head. A young princess named Gandhari, from the land of Gandhara, has been promised to a prince of the Kurus. Then she learns that he is blind. She takes a cloth, folds it, and binds her own eyes. Before we get to why, see the boys grow up.
screen: `A CLOTH, FOLDED MANY TIMES.` → `A PROMISED PRINCESS.` → `SHE BINDS HER OWN EYES.`

segments.voice: With the three boys born, the text says, the land of the Kurus flourishes: rains on time, full harvests, cities busy and safe. Bhishma raises the princes as his own. Dhritarashtra, the text says, becomes the strongest; Pandu, the finest archer; and Vidura has no equal in knowing dharma. Then, who rules? Dhritarashtra is the eldest, but the text says his blindness passes him over. Vidura is wise, but his mother was a servant, so he's passed over too. The crown goes to Pandu, the younger. Some readers find, in a firstborn watching his younger brother take the throne, a seed of much that follows. Now Bhishma looks for wives. He hears of Gandhari, daughter of the king of Gandhara, and asks for her for Dhritarashtra. Her family hesitates over a blind groom, then agrees. When Gandhari hears, she binds her eyes, resolving, the text says, out of regard for her husband, never to have more than he has. Her brother, Shakuni, brings her to Hastinapura. Remember his name. Readers take the blindfold more than one way. Some see a wife's complete devotion. Some see a woman refusing to be the one who sees, in a marriage she didn't choose. Some see grief worn on the face. The text gives the reason in her husband's honor and leaves the rest of her silent. Now two people who cannot see sit beside the throne, one by birth and one by choice, and a pale king sits on it.
screen: `THE KURU LAND FLOURISHES.` · `THE CROWN GOES TO PANDU.` · `GANDHARI BINDS HER EYES.` · `SHAKUNI BRINGS HER HOME.`

segments.voice: If it's comfortable, let the eyes close or rest low. Gandhari chose to share what her husband couldn't have; sit a moment without sight and notice what fills the space: sounds, the floor, the air. Then bring to mind someone close who carries a loss or a limit you don't, and just sit beside it.
Gandhari, the princess who bound her own eyes, out of regard for the blind husband she married, Dhritarashtra.
Your line: a strip of cloth, folded and tied. A bride's answer to a blind groom. That's day seven hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: In Hindu retellings Gandhari is remembered as a figure of pativrata, devotion to a husband, and the blindfold is the image tellers and painters use for her.
